summary.text: One of Penelope's suitors in Apollodorus' catalogue of the fifty-seven wooers from Dulichium — a namesake of Eurypylus king of Cos and of other bearers of the name in Greek epic.

story.text: Apollodorus names Eurypylus among the suitors who devoured Odysseus' substance, listed after Agenor and before Pylaemenes in the long company of Penelope's wooers.
Distinct from Eurypylus son of Euaemon, lord of Ormenion in the Iliad (`eurypylus-euaemonid`), and from Eurypylus king of Cos (`eurypylus-cos`).
Distinct also from Eurypylus son of Telephus, the Mysian who killed Peneleos at Troy and was slain by Neoptolemus (`eurypylus-telephus`).
